Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

weapon noun

also weapons, arms, toy weapon, take up arms, lay down arms, by force of arms, be under arms, be armed, turn in weapons, hand over weapons, arms race, armaments, defensive and offensive weapons, disarm

classical

Publil. Sent. E 11
Cic. Mil. 11: esse cum tēlō hominis occīdendī causā (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 186

tēlum, tēlī n.

noun, second declension

a weapon; properly one that is thrown

Properly a missile, a spear or a dart; then any weapon for striking, a sword or an axe (Lewis & Short). Weapons in general are arma.

Other words

  • arma, armōrum n. pl. — arms, weapons; armour

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 3.12.19; Traupman 185, 188

    Plural only: properly the arms for defence and close fighting, then weapons of every kind (Lewis & Short). To take up arms, arma capere; to hand in one’s weapons, arma trādere (Traupman 185, 188).

Examples

  • Ēripere tēlum, nōn dare īrātō decet.

    Take the weapon away from an angry man; don’t hand it to him.Publil. Sent. E 11

  • ūsus equī nunc est, levibus nunc lūditur armīs, nunc pila, nunc celerī volvitur orbe trochus

    now is the time for riding, now for games with light weapons, now for the ball, now the hoop goes rolling roundOv. Tr. 3.12.19–20

  • arma capere

    to take up armsTraupman 185

  • ab armīs discēdere

    to lay down armsTraupman 185; cf. Caes. BG 5.41.8 (Lewis & Short s.v. discēdō)

  • vī et armīs

    by force of armsTraupman 185

  • in armīs esse

    to be under arms, be armedTraupman 185

  • arma trādere

    to hand over one’s weaponsTraupman 188; cf. Caes. BG 1.27: armīs trāditīs (Lewis & Short s.v. trādō)

  • aliquem armīs exuere

    to disarm someoneTraupman 186; cf. Caes. BG 5.51: hostem armīs (Lewis & Short s.v. exuō)

  • tēla ad tegendum et ad nocendum

    defensive and offensive weaponsTraupman 186

  • apparātus bellī

    armaments, the equipment of warTraupman 185, 184

  • armōrum certāmen

    an arms race (literally “a contest of arms”)Traupman 184, 185

See also sword, shield, war, soldier, toy.
